profile.constituencyprofile_Text:
Thamballapalle lies in the western part of Annamayya district, Andhra Pradesh, and is one of the key assembly segments under the Rajampet Lok Sabha constituency. It spans six mandals—Thamballapalle, Mulakalacheruvu, Peddamandyam, Kurabalakota, Peddathippasamudram, and B. Kothakota—with a total population of approximately 2.74 lakh. The scenic Horsley Hills hill station, and the renowned Rishi Valley School. These sites contribute to the constituency’s tourism potential, alongside emerging opportunities in services and small-scale industries.


The constituency is predominantly agrarian, with agriculture contributing 61.23% to the local economy. It benefits from irrigation projects like the Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi (HNSS) Canal and the Mudivedu Reservoir, which support cultivation across a variety of red, loamy, and black soils. Key crops include groundnut, millets, and horticultural produce, sustaining a large rural population.

economy_text.economy_Text:
Economy at a Glance

Thamballapalle’s economy is heavily agriculture-centric, with the Agricultural & Allied Sector contributing a dominant 61.24% to the local GCDP. This is supported by fertile red, loamy, and black soils, and irrigation from the Handri-Neeva Canal and Mudivedu Reservoir, enabling the cultivation of groundnut, millets, pulses, vegetables, and horticultural crops.

The Industries Sector, contributing 14.93%, is gradually expanding with opportunities in agro-processing, local manufacturing, and MSMEs, especially along the NH-42 corridor. Small-scale industries related to food processing, brick-making, and construction materials are emerging drivers.

The Service Sector makes up 23.83% of the economy, led by education, retail, transport, and tourism services. With growing interest in eco and heritage tourism—attractions like Horsley Hills and Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple—the service sector holds strong potential for future growth.


Agriculture drives over 60% of the local economy, supported by irrigation from Handri-Neeva and Mudivedu Reservoir. Promoting high-value crops like mango, guava, and vegetables, alongside organic and precision farming, can boost productivity and farmer incomes.

With attractions like Horsley Hills and Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple, Thamballapalle has strong potential for eco and heritage tourism. Developing basic infrastructure, homestays, and nature trails can drive rural employment and local revenue. Agro-processing, packaging, and small-scale manufacturing (bricks, food products) can thrive with NH-42 connectivity. Supporting local entrepreneurship and value-addition industries will diversify the economy and create jobs.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Thamballapalle is poised for steady economic progress with a targeted 13% annual GCDP growth rate driven by key sectors such as agriculture, agro-processing, eco-tourism, and rural services. This growth path supports the constituency’s vision of fostering a resilient and inclusive rural economy while preserving its natural and cultural heritage by 2047.
